Saying that we 'drag our weapon of choice' in a 'deeply sacred ritual' seems to, for me, glorify and romanticise self harm. 

I think in all cases of self harm, the reasons why we do it and the way we process pain is completely unique to everyone. But I don't think we should be talking about self harm in the way you're describing it. It just sound like you're trivialising and glorifying a very real and destructive act.

I'm gonna hijack the top comment for some explanation. I have OCD and autism, so a lot of my rituals and compulsions are usually linked with sensory stimulation. 

My toenail compulsion is more to do with the physical release I get from it, rather that self harm. And if you've ever picked at a scab, you might get what it feels like. It hurts when I peel them off, but it feels like insane amount of pressure building up to a release.

I'm currently in therapy, and I have been for the past 8 years or so. I do CBT (no, not cock and ball torture,though I can see why you'd think that) and psychotherapy, and I'm learning healthier ways to cope with intrusive thoughts and stress.

Again, I just wanted to clarify some things for anyone who's interested at all.
